title: Patch: the dev dashboard's audit reads pages and filters by who and what
thread:
**Issue #4168 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4168: Patch: the dev dashboard's audit reads pages and filters by who and what
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Today the audit page shows the newest 200 admin actions as raw data with only a Refresh button. Once it is built, a maintainer can page back past those 200 and narrow the list to one account or one kind of action. Someone asking “who revoked that invite code on Tuesday” gets an answer in seconds instead of scrolling through hundreds of entries. This matters more once the moderation tools also write their bans, revocations and redemption pauses to the audit, since that history is exactly what the page exists to inspect.

## Why

The spec promises an audit row for every dev and admin action that the dashboard can read, but the read side is a dead end: the endpoint answers the newest 200 rows and nothing older is reachable, and the page offers no search. The row count is a single hard-coded page size, the response carries no cursor, and the UI has only Refresh. Volume is about to grow, because the open moderation-audit work will add a row per ban, revocation and redemption pause.

## Proposal

Give the audit read a cursor (`before_id`, default page size stays 200) and optional filters for acting account and route, in both store backends; expose them on the endpoint; add a filter row and an Older pager to the dashboard page. Update the §14.10 audit paragraph to describe paging and filtering. No new ruling: this is dev tooling with no game-semantics decision in it.

## Where it lands

- `crates/server/src/api/admin.rs` (`get_audit`), `crates/server/src/admin/store.rs`, the Postgres and fake implementations behind it, `crates/server/src/config.rs` (page size)
- `apps/admin/src/api.ts`, `apps/admin/src/types.ts`, `apps/admin/src/Audit.tsx` (plus test ids and tests)
- SPEC §14.10 (`spec/14-economy.md`, R3074000's paragraphs)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reading the audit with no params still returns the newest page as today
- [ ] A second read with the returned cursor returns the next older page with no gaps or repeats
- [ ] Filtering by acting account and by route returns only matching rows, in both store backends
- [ ] The dashboard page offers the filters and a pager, covered by its tests
- [ ] The §14.10 text describes paging and filtering, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes

## Size and risks

Small-medium: one endpoint, two store backends, one page. Risk is low; the audit stays server-only and append-only, so nothing about retention changes. Rejected alternative: full-text search over the JSON blobs — overkill for a handful of devs; exact account and route filters answer the real questions.

---

Class: `polish` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44244028876)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Give the dev dashboard's audit read a cursor (`before_id`, page size stays `ADMIN_AUDIT_PAGE` = 200) and exact-match filters for acting account (`profile_id`) and route (`route`), in both store backends and on the endpoint; add a filter row and an Older pager to the dashboard's Audit section; and describe paging and filtering in the §14.10 audit paragraph. No new ruling: this is dev tooling with no game-semantics decision, so no note under `spec/rulings/`, no file under `spec/pending/`, and no test or comment citing `R4168`.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/server/src/admin/store.rs` | change | New `AdminActionFilter` struct; new `Tx::admin_actions_page`; `pg` + `fake` implementations; `admin_actions_recent` delegates to it |
| `crates/server/src/api/admin.rs` | change | `get_audit` parses `before_id`, `profile_id`, `route`; answers `{ actions, nextBeforeId }`; module + function docs |
| `crates/server/src/config.rs` | change | Doc comment on `ADMIN_AUDIT_PAGE` only; value stays 200 |
| `crates/server/README.md` | change | `/api/admin/audit` row: query params and `nextBeforeId` |
| `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` | change | One new test in `mod dev_dashboard` (runs against both backends) |
| `crates/server/tests/api/admin.rs` | change | New endpoint tests |
| `apps/admin/src/types.ts` | change | `AuditResponse` gains `nextBeforeId: number \| null` |
| `apps/admin/src/api.ts` | change | `audit()` takes optional `{ beforeId, profileId, route }` |
| `apps/admin/src/Audit.tsx` | change | Filter row (account, route, Apply, Clear) and Older pager |
| `apps/admin/src/testids.ts` | change | Five new testids (below) |
| `apps/admin/src/test/canned.ts` | change | `AUDIT` fixture gains `nextBeforeId` |
| `apps/admin/src/api.test.ts` | change | Parameter URL cases |
| `apps/admin/src/Dashboard.test.tsx` | change | New Audit filter/pager tests |
| `apps/admin/README.md` | change | Audit bullet and test-id list |
| `spec/14-economy.md` | change | §14.10 dashboard paragraph only |

Must not touch: anything under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`; `crates/server/migrations/` (no schema change: `admin_actions_at_idx` and `admin_actions_profile_idx` from migration 0080 already cover the read); `crates/engine`, `crates/cards`, `crates/ai`, `crates/shared`, `crates/run`; `apps/web`, `apps/edge`; `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md` (the daily fold owns them); `spec/pending/`, `spec/rulings/` (no ruling). Governing spec: §14.10 and §14.11; existing ruling `R3074000` (cited, not amended).

## Steps

1. **`crates/server/src/admin/store.rs`: add the filter type.** Beside `AdminAction`, add `#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)] pub struct AdminActionFilter { pub before_id: Option<i64>, pub profile_id: Option<String>, pub route: Option<String> }`. Document: `before_id` is an exclusive upper bound on the row id; `profile_id` and `route` are exact matches; `None` (and, by the time it reaches the store, never an empty string) means no constraint.
2. **`store.rs`: add `Tx::admin_actions_page`.** Signature `pub async fn admin_actions_page(&mut self, filter: &AdminActionFilter, limit: i64) -> StoreResult<Vec<AdminAction>>`, dispatching through the existing `admin_dispatch!` macro to `pg::actions_page` / `fake::actions_page`. Keep `admin_actions_recent(limit)` and implement it as `self.admin_actions_page(&AdminActionFilter::default(), limit)` so its three existing contract callers are untouched.
3. **`store.rs` `pg`: filter in SQL.** `select id, profile_id, route, request, before_value, after_value, at from public.admin_actions where ($2::bigint is null or id < $2) and ($3::text is null or profile_id::text = $3) and ($4::text is null or route = $4) order by at desc, id desc limit $1::bigint`, binding `limit`, `filter.before_id`, `filter.profile_id`, `filter.route`. Comparing `profile_id::text` (instead of `$3::uuid`) means any garbage string matches nothing instead of erroring, so no new error path. Ordering is unchanged.
4. **`store.rs` `fake`: same predicates in memory.** Clone the table, keep rows where `filter.before_id.is_none_or(|b| row.id < b)`, `filter.profile_id.as_ref().is_none_or(|p| row.profile_id.as_deref() == Some(p))` (a row whose account was deleted has `profile_id: None` and matches no account filter), and `filter.route.as_ref().is_none_or(|r| &row.route == r)`, then the existing `newest_first` and `take(limit)`.
5. **`crates/server/src/api/admin.rs`: parse the query in `get_audit`.** Read `before_id` with the `query_number` pattern from `crates/server/src/api/replays.rs`: absent means newest page; present must parse as `i64` or return `bad_request("before_id must be a whole number")`. Read `profile_id` and `route` via `req.query.get(..)`, trim them, and map empty/missing to `None`. Call `tx.admin_actions_page(&filter, ADMIN_AUDIT_PAGE)`. The `usernames_of` lookup and row rendering stay exactly as today.
6. **`admin.rs`: answer the cursor.** Build `nextBeforeId: Option<i64>` as the last returned action's `id` when `actions.len() as i64 == ADMIN_AUDIT_PAGE`, else `None` (a short page means the history is exhausted; a following read then answers `[]` and `null`). Answer `json!({ "actions": actions, "nextBeforeId": nextBeforeId })`. Update the module bullet (`- GET /api/admin/audit (R3074000)`) and `get_audit`'s doc comment to name the three query params, the fixed page size, and `nextBeforeId`.
7. **`crates/server/src/config.rs` + `crates/server/README.md`.** On `ADMIN_AUDIT_PAGE`, extend the doc comment: it is the page size of every `GET /api/admin/audit` read, newest rows first. In the README's `/api/admin/audit` row, document `?before_id=<id>&profile_id=<id>&route=<METHOD path>` (all optional, exact matches, `before_id` exclusive) and the response `{ actions: [...], nextBeforeId: <id> | null }`.
8. **`apps/admin/src/types.ts` + `api.ts`.** Change `AuditResponse` to `{ actions: AuditAction[]; nextBeforeId: number | null }`. Change `audit` to `audit: (query?: { beforeId?: number; profileId?: string; route?: string }) => call<AuditResponse>(path)` where `path` is `/api/admin/audit` plus a `URLSearchParams` (`before_id`, `profile_id`, `route`, skipping `undefined` and `""`) only when at least one is present — so bare `audit()` still requests exactly `/api/admin/audit` and the existing `api.test.ts` row keeps passing.
9. **`apps/admin/src/testids.ts`.** Add `auditProfile: "admin-audit-profile"`, `auditRoute: "admin-audit-route"`, `auditApply: "admin-audit-apply"`, `auditClear: "admin-audit-clear"`, `auditOlder: "admin-audit-older"` in the Audit block.
10. **`apps/admin/src/Audit.tsx`: filters and pager.** Keep Refresh and the table. Add state: `profileInput`/`routeInput` strings, committed `applied: { profileId, route }`, accumulated `actions: AuditAction[]`, `next: number | null`, `loading: boolean`, `error: string | null`. Add `loadPage(beforeId: number | undefined, mode: "replace" | "append")` calling `api.audit({ beforeId, profileId: applied.profileId || undefined, route: applied.route || undefined })`; on success replace or append `actions` and set `next` from `nextBeforeId`; on failure set `error` via `messageOf`. A `useEffect` on `[api, revision, asked, applied]` calls `loadPage(undefined, "replace")`. Render a filter row (two text inputs, Apply sets `applied` from inputs, Clear empties both and resets `applied`), and an Older button (`auditOlder`) shown only when `next !== null`, disabled while loading, calling `loadPage(next, "append")`. Refresh keeps working and resets to the first page.
11. **`apps/admin/src/test/canned.ts`.** Add `nextBeforeId: 6` to the `AUDIT` fixture (its oldest action has `id: 6`). Leave `dashboardRoutes()`'s `"GET /api/admin/audit"` key as the first page; per-test overrides will add filtered/paged URLs.
12. **`spec/14-economy.md` §14.10.** Extend the sentence "Every dev tool and dashboard write leaves an audit row, who, which route, the request, the values before and after, and when, which the dashboard reads and no player does ([[R3074000]])." with two sentences: the dashboard reads the newest `ADMIN_AUDIT_PAGE` rows first and follows `nextBeforeId` with `before_id` for older pages; `profile_id` and `route` narrow the read to one acting account or one route. Keep every existing `[[…]]` link; add none.
13. **`apps/admin/README.md`.** Update the Audit bullet (filter row, Older pager) and append the five new testids to the test-id list.

## Tests

- `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`, `mod dev_dashboard`: new test `audit_pages_by_cursor_and_filter` (NOT `r4168_…`: an `r<n>` name with no ruling note fails `spec check`). Seed five rows across two profiles and two routes with distinct `at`; assert `admin_actions_page(&default, 2)` returns the newest two newest-first; a second read with `before_id` = last id returns the next two with no overlap; a third returns the last one; `profile_id` filter returns only that account's rows; `route` filter only that route; both combined; `before_id` below the oldest id returns `[]`. Runs against both backends through the existing harness.
- `crates/server/tests/api/admin.rs`: new `audit_read_pages_by_cursor_and_filters` — after several dev writes, `GET /api/admin/audit` is 200 with `actions` newest-first plus `nextBeforeId`; `GET /api/admin/audit?before_id=<last id>` returns disjoint older rows; `?profile_id=<dev>` and `?route=PUT /api/admin/rating` return only matching rows; `?before_id=abc` is 400. Extend the existing `r3074000_…` read test's assertions only to also expect `nextBeforeId` present (do not rename it).
- `apps/admin/src/api.test.ts`: add `CASES` rows — `audit` with `{ beforeId: 6, profileId: "p", route: "PUT /api/admin/rating" }` sends `GET /api/admin/audit?before_id=6&profile_id=p&route=PUT+%2Fapi%2Fadmin%2Frating`; `audit` with `{}` sends exactly `/api/admin/audit`.
- `apps/admin/src/Dashboard.test.tsx`, `describe("Audit")`: "Apply sends the filters and replaces the list" (override `"GET /api/admin/audit?profile_id=…&route=…"` with one row; assert rows replaced and the unfiltered URL was requested once); "Older appends the next page, then hides" (first page `nextBeforeId: 6`, override `"GET /api/admin/audit?before_id=6"` with the older rows and `nextBeforeId: null`; click Older; assert four rows then no Older button); "Clear empties the filters and reads the newest page again".
- Commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::admin`, `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store dev_dashboard`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `pnpm --dir apps/admin exec vitest run src/api.test.ts src/Dashboard.test.tsx`, `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] No-param audit read returns the newest page exactly as today, plus `nextBeforeId`.
- [ ] A second read with the returned cursor returns the next older page with no gaps or repeats.
- [ ] `profile_id` and `route` filters return only matching rows in both store backends.
- [ ] The dashboard offers account/route filters and an Older pager, covered by its tests.
- [ ] §14.10 describes paging and filtering; `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] Only the checks above run: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy on `jackioh-server`, the two server test targets, the two admin test files, `spec check`. No `#[ignore]`, no weakened test, no new allow/lint suppression.

## Risks

- Cursor vs ordering: the read stays ordered by `(at desc, id desc)` while the cursor bounds `id` alone. This is gap-free whenever `at` is non-decreasing across writes (the `at` is stamped at write time and the identity `id` is assigned in write order); a clock stepping backward between two writes could hide one row across a page boundary. Accepted: the audit is low-volume dev tooling and the previous read had no cursor at all.
- `profile_id::text = $3` cannot use the uuid index; fine for a dashboard-only table with hundreds of rows.
- `revision` prop resets the Audit list to the first page on any successful dashboard write; that matches the section's existing refresh behavior.

## Open questions

None. Filter semantics (exact `profile_id` and full `route` string, empty means absent) and cursor semantics (exclusive `before_id`, `nextBeforeId` null when exhausted) are set above; the rejected alternatives were username-substring search and full-text search over the JSON blobs (overkill per the issue) and a composite `(at, id)` cursor (overkill for dev tooling).
```
